title: The phone app reads Hevy and Strong export files with a spreadsheet library that has two known serious flaws
what: When a member brings in workouts from Hevy or Strong, the phone opens the file they picked with spreadsheet library version 0.18.5. The dependency scan marks two high-severity flaws in that version: one lets a crafted file tamper with the app's internal objects, the other lets a crafted file freeze the reader. There is no fixed version on the public package registry, so the scan offers no automatic upgrade. The risk is limited because the member picks their own file.
expected: The importer uses a spreadsheet reader with no known high-severity flaws, as the gym panel already does with its newer copy.
who: members who import workouts from Hevy or Strong
how_often: only when a member imports a crafted file
fix_line: Move the phone app to the spreadsheet library's own newer release (the one the gym panel already uses), then re-run the import tests.

title: The phone app's screen-navigation library is flagged high by the dependency scan
what: The library that moves the phone app between screens is marked high severity by the dependency scan, through a link-reading package it pulls in. The scan says the fix needs a major upgrade of that library. Every screen in this area uses it, including the gym's workout of the day and the import card.
expected: The navigation library has no high-severity alerts, or the alert is checked and written down as not reachable in this app.
how_often: unknown; depends on whether a crafted link can reach it
fix_line: Check whether the flagged link-reading path is reachable; if it is, plan the major navigation upgrade with the next app dependency bump.

items.reason: The only server call reached from this area is the member's workout-of-the-day read (member_gym_wod). It runs as owner with a fixed search path, is open to anon and signed-in callers by design, and only answers for the gym tied to the member's own key; everything else in the area works on the phone's own database.

Table gym_wods: apps cannot read it at all (row rules on, no policies, all rights taken from anon and signed-in users); the only way in is member_gym_wod, and test 6e/6f proves a member of another gym gets only their own gym's workout. No other server table is touched by this area.
Rule applied: the one table this area touches (gym_wods) has a cross-gym test, so no finding.
Rule applied: no live cross-gym attempt was run; only the existing database test was read.
No key pattern hits in this area's files in the secrets scan, and the area's files hold no keys; the only web address is the public exercise-clip download folder.
No AI or paid-service key is used by any file in this area; the Hevy reader needs no account or key.
No sign-in, PIN or session handling in these workout components.

Text boxes (search, workout name and note, weigh-in, edit-session, log-past) feed an in-memory filter or the phone's own database through placeholder-bound queries, and are shown back as plain text, never as web page code. The Hevy link box is rebuilt to a fixed hevy.com address before the hidden browser opens it, and that browser refuses any other site.
Nothing in this area uploads. The before-and-after picture is made on the phone from cached copies and leaves only through the share menu when the member taps Share.
No gym link or join code is made or opened here. The gym's workout is read with the member's own private key, not a link; the only link is a public Hevy share link the member pastes.

The area's libraries: picture, video and web-view libraries have no alerts; the navigation library is flagged high; the spreadsheet reader behind the import card (0.18.5) has two high alerts with no fixed version in the registry.
